raw_plan.original_behavior: Allocates 16 bytes via malloc; exits(1) if allocation fails; computes strlen(input)+1 and memcpy's that many bytes into the 16-byte buffer regardless of size; then calls puts on the buffer and frees it; returns void.
raw_plan.required_invariant: The number of bytes copied into the 16-byte heap buffer must not exceed 16, i.e. strlen(input)+1 <= 16, so the copy writes at most capacity-1 bytes plus a NUL terminator.
raw_plan.repair_strategy: After computing the length via strlen, compare strlen(input)+1 against the 16-byte capacity; if it exceeds capacity, reject the oversized input by freeing the buffer and calling exit(1) (or otherwise failing safely) without performing the overflowing memcpy; otherwise perform the original memcpy, puts, and free sequence unchanged.
raw_plan.failure_behavior: On oversized input, free the allocated buffer and terminate via exit(1) without copying, preserving no overflow; on malloc failure, exit(1) as originally.
raw_plan.expected_behavior: For valid inputs with strlen(input)+1 <= 16, behavior is identical to the original: allocate 16 bytes, copy the string including NUL, print it with puts, free it, and return. For oversized inputs, the function rejects the input by freeing the buffer and exiting with status 1, never writing beyond the 16-byte allocation.

strlen(input)+1 > 16 path performs no memcpy into the buffer and terminates via exit(1) after freeing
malloc failure path still calls exit(1)
no write occurs beyond offset 15 of the 16-byte heap allocation
